_note: Draft English rendering of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Vayikra 23, generated by scripts/translate_tafsir_english.py against the JA (not the biblical Hebrew). Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.2: Command the sons of Israel and say to them: the festivals of God, which you are obligated to designate by special names — these are My festivals.
translations.3: Six days shall labors be performed, and on the seventh day is a desisting — it is a Sabbath, a consecrated name; no labor shall you perform. Such is the Sabbath of God, in all your dwellings.
translations.4: These are the festivals of God, which are designated by special names, which you are obligated to designate in their appointed times.
translations.5: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of it, between the two sunsets — a Passover offering to God.
translations.6: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the festival of unleavened bread to God; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
translations.7: On the first day of it, a consecrated name shall be for you; no labor for profit shall you perform.
translations.8: And offer an offering to God during these seven days; and on the seventh day, a consecrated name — no labor for profit shall you perform.
translations.9: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.10: Command the sons of Israel and say to them: when you enter the land which I am giving you, and you reap its harvest, bring a sheaf of the first of your harvest to the priest.
translations.11: And he shall wave it before God, so that it be accepted from you; and its waving shall be on the morrow after the rest-day.
translations.12: And offer, on the day of your waving of it, an unblemished lamb, a year old, as an ascent-offering to God.
translations.13: And with it, from wheat, two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil — an offering acceptable and pleasing to God; and its libation of wine, a quarter of a qist.
translations.14: And bread, and parched grain, and roasted grain, you shall not eat until this very day — until you bring the offering of your Lord. A decree forever, throughout the passing of your generations, in all your dwellings.
translations.15: And count for yourselves, from the morrow after the rest-day, from the day you brought the sheaf of the waving — seven complete weeks shall there be.
translations.16: Until the morrow of the seventh week; and the total of what you count shall be fifty days. And offer a new offering to God.
translations.17: That you bring from your dwellings bread for waving — two loaves, of two-tenths of fine flour shall they be; leavened shall they be baked. They are first-fruits to God.
translations.18: And offer with the two loaves seven unblemished lambs, yearlings, and a bull from the cattle, and two rams — they shall be an ascent-offering to God; and their grain-offering and their libations — an offering acceptable and pleasing to God.
translations.19: And offer also a he-goat from the goats for the purification, and two yearling lambs for the well-being sacrifice.
translations.20: And the priest shall wave what is required of them, together with the two first-fruit loaves, as a waving before God, over the two lambs; and they shall be a holy portion to God, given over to the priest.
translations.21: And designate that very day by a consecrated name — it shall be for you; no labor for profit shall you perform. A decree forever, in all your dwellings, throughout your generations.
translations.22: And when you reap the harvest of your fields, do not cut to the very edge of your estate in your reaping, and the scattered grain of your sowing do not glean — rather, for the poor and the stranger, leave them. I am God your Lord; I shall recompense you with good.
translations.23: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.24: Command the sons of Israel, saying: on the first day of the seventh month, there shall be for you a rest-day and a sounding of clamor — a consecrated name.
translations.25: No labor for profit shall you perform; and offer an additional offering to God.
translations.26: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.27: Now on the tenth day of this seventh month — and it is the Day of Atonement — a consecrated name shall be for you; and starve yourselves, and offer an additional offering to God.
translations.28: And no work at all shall you perform on this very day, for it is a day of atonement for you, on which pardon is sought on your behalf before God your Lord.
translations.29: And every adult person who does not fast on this very day shall be cut off from his people.
translations.30: And every person who performs any labor on this very day — I shall destroy that person from among his people.
translations.31: And no labor at all shall you perform. A decree forever, throughout your generations, in all your dwellings.
translations.32: It is a desisting — a Sabbath for you; and you shall starve yourselves, from the evening of the ninth of this month until the second evening, you shall cease your work.
translations.33: Then God spoke to Moses, speaking.
translations.34: Command the sons of Israel, saying: on the fifteenth day of the seventh month is the festival of booths — seven days to God.
translations.35: On the first day, a consecrated name; no labor for profit shall you perform.
translations.36: And during these seven days you shall offer an offering to God; and on the eighth day, a consecrated name shall be for you — and offer an additional offering to God, and remain in its holiness; and no labor for profit shall you perform.
translations.37: These are the festivals of God, which you are obligated to designate by special names, and in which you shall offer offerings to God — ascent-offering and grain-offering, and sacrifice and libation, the obligation of each day in its day.
translations.38: Apart from the Sabbaths of God, and apart from your gifts, and your vows, and your freewill-offerings, which you give to God.
translations.39: Now on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, at the season of your gathering in the yield of the land, you shall make a pilgrimage-festival to God for seven days; on the first day of them a rest-day, and on the eighth day a rest-day.
translations.40: And take for yourselves on the first day, from the fruit of the citron tree, and from the fronds of the palm, and from the branches of the myrtle-wood braided together, and from the willows of the valley — and rejoice with them before God your Lord, seven days.
translations.41: And celebrate it as a festival to God, seven days in the year — a decree forever throughout your generations; in the seventh month you shall celebrate it.
translations.42: And dwell in the booths seven days at My command; every native-born of the house of Israel shall dwell in the booths —
translations.43: so that your generations may know that I, God your Lord, sheltered the sons of Israel in the shade of My clouds when I brought them out from the land of Egypt. I am God your Lord, true to My promise.
translations.44: And Moses addressed the sons of Israel concerning the festivals of God.
